- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot upward trends.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.40) — model fails to capture sharp downside moves.
- Lag in price corrections: model often delays mean reversion, especially after strong sentiment shifts.
- Overshoot after spikes: model overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes, leading to exaggerated peaks.
- Mean reversion bias: model underestimates downward correction after prolonged upward runs.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early summer (June) when sentiment is volatile and market is consolidating.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.10, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence; if sentiment < -0.30, increase forecast by 5–10% to compensate for underreaction.
